Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helix is excited about the private-deploy routing and the fallback model variants you showed. We want to run a focused "solution readiness" audit so our architects can validate operational fit before we commit to the POC.

High-level asks from our side:
- Reference topology for a VPC Private deployment (network flows, egress constraints)
- Expected token-latency profile for the 2k context model under continuous-batch workload
- Observability hooks (what tracing/span IDs to expect and where logs land)
- Any constraints for KV-cache warm starts when rehydrating from snapshot

Can you put together a short checklist and a 1-hour architecture review call this week? We'll share our internal infra diagram and a short runbook.

Attachments: none in this message.

Best,
Nina Park

Looping in a couple technical clarifications I want documented before the call so we don't waste cycles:

1) Model variants: which model families will Helix plan to serve? We need to know max seq len, expected concurrent streams, and typical prompt shaping to recommend batching windows and cache policies.

2) Networking: any custom firewall/NAC rules that would block long-lived TLS sessions or gRPC keepalives? Private deployments assume stable sockets for KV cache eviction efficiency.

3) Data residency & certs: if they want an on-prem package, we need their cert rotation cadence and whether an HSM is required for key material.

4) Acceptance criteria for latency: is 99th percentile <= 200ms for <512 tokens acceptable, or do they need stricter SLOs?

If Nina can send an internal infra diagram and expected traffic profile (RPS and burst), we'll produce a short "readiness audit" doc and a checklist before the call.

- Prio (Engineering, Redwood)

From: Nina Park <nina.park@helix.consult>

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:20 AM priyom.das@redwood.ai wrote:
> Looping in a couple technical clarifications I want documented before the call so we don't waste cycles:
>
> 1) Model variants: which model families will Helix plan to serve? ...

Thanks — quick answers inline and our attachments: Helix "mini-architecture" (PDF) and traffic sample (xlsx).

1) Model families: Helix will start with an open LLM (gpt-lite-2k) for customer-facing notes and a smaller emb-only model for search. Max seq len ~2048, expected steady-state concurrent streams = 30 across two AZs, peak bursts ~120 RPS for short windows.

2) Networking: We run a VPC with strict egress through a transit gateway. Long-lived TLS sessions are fine; we will avoid NAT timeouts by keeping session timeouts > 30m. We will provide a list of firewall rules that can be opened for Redwood's control-plane endpoints.

3) Data residency & certs: We rotate certs quarterly; HSM not required for initial POC. We can support AWS KMS.

4) Latency expectations: We can target 99p <= 250ms for <512 tokens for the POC; if Redwood recommends a tighter SLO we'll review.

Attachments: helix-arch-v1.pdf (mini-architecture), redwood-helix-map.xlsx (sample traffic profile).

We'll take Tue 5/4 10:00 PT for the call. Invite sent.

—Nina
Partner Engineering Lead — Helix Consulting

Forwarding Helix's notes and attachments. Quick internal plan from our side before tomorrow's call:

Action items
- Prio: produce a 1-pager "readiness audit" showing reference VPC topology, required firewall rules, and KV-cache warm start recommendations (owner: priyom_das; due: Tue 5/4 08:00 PT).
- Marissa: prepare a short perf memo with our baseline for gpt-lite-2k at 2k context (include continuous batching vs. strict low-latency mode). Bring example traces to show 99p behavior (due: Tue 5/4 08:00 PT).
- Laura: draft POC acceptance criteria and a proposed kickoff deck (owners, timeline, go/no-go) (due: Wed 5/5 12:00 PT).
- Sergio: commercial alignment — prepare a one-slide remark on expected commitment levels to unblock Dedicated offering if they want reserved capacity (due: Wed 5/5).

Notes: Helix's peak burst (120 RPS) and session timeout policy looks fine; key unknowns are their exact prompt shapes and how many long-lived conversations will maintain hot KV caches. We should push for a small synthetic run during POC to validate prefix cache hit rates.

I'll own scheduling follow-ups with Helix and share our readiness audit before the call. If anyone sees additional checklist items, reply-all.

-Karthik
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
